findings.reason: §6 should state whether the supervisor spawn extends `placement.py`'s placement path (routing its `srun` client into the batch step) or replaces it, which is the first decision its implementation node will face.
findings.text: §6 routes worker launch through a new supervisor `spawn` request and never cites `reckon/crew/placement.py`, whose `placement_argv` (placement.py:326), `step_prefix` (placement.py:231) and `reservation_step_argv` (placement.py:840) already place a worker as an overlapping step of the held allocation; a plan that adds a launch path without naming the existing one risks a second placement seam beside the owner the followup f-aslf-010 is already trying to retire into

findings.reason: without naming the surviving owner (reckon's `placement.py`, whose `_adopt_live_fleet_allocation` at placement.py:488 already bridges to `fleet_node.recorded_job_id()`) an implementation node keeps both records and the duplicate lock, the exact drift §6 exists to close.
findings.text: the one fleet allocation carries two records and two locks that cannot serialise it: `placement.py:reservation_path()` publishes `crew_home()/placement/reservation.json` guarded by `_reservation_hold_lock` (placement.py:115, on `reservation.lock`) while `fleet_node.publish_record()` (fleet_node.py:305) writes `~/.local/state/fleet/record.json` and `dotfiles/bin/cx:fleet_ensure` (bin/cx:237-244) takes its own `flock` on `~/.local/state/fleet/hold.lock` with a third `submitted` state file; §2 (plan.html#s2) resolves the fleet from the fleet-node record and §6 (plan.html#s6) says "Both must move to the supervisor-running allocation" without naming which of the two record/lock owners survives

findings.reason: the plan's stated outcome ("Both must move to the supervisor-running allocation") is unsatisfiable until it names the `salloc` path as the one retired, since a plan that leaves both live holds two allocations.
findings.text: two mechanisms hold the same allocation: `ensure_reservation` submits with `RESERVATION_SCHEDULER="salloc"` + `--no-shell` (placement.py:52,417), which has no batch step, while `fleet_node.submit`/`generate_hold_script` (fleet_node.py:164,123) submits with `sbatch` so the batch step runs `fleet-supervisor`; §6 (plan.html#s6) acknowledges "reckon's re-hold path creates an allocation with salloc --no-shell, which has no batch step at all" but does not name which mechanism is retired

findings.reason: §2 should delegate the whole hold to `reckon fleet-node hold`/`placement.ensure_reservation` and keep only the viewer in `cx`, or state why a login-side lock is needed beside the allocation-wide one.
findings.text: the plan places the idempotent hold in `cx`, which re-implements the resolve/confirm/wait loop (`bin/cx:239` `flock -w 900` on its own lock, a 180-iteration `squeue` poll at bin/cx:258, its own `submitted` file) directly over the same scheduler query the owner `ensure_reservation` (placement.py:417) performs, with no justification in §2 for why the owner cannot carry the one guarantee; a login-side copy of the owner's lock is what `placement.py`'s `_reservation_hold_lock` docstring exists to prevent

findings.reason: the sections must account for the added surface in their own text: retire the `srun` viewer (keeping only the ssh route §8 proved stable) and state what `fleet-sessions`/`CX_FLEET_VIA` retires or why nothing can be.
findings.text: with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, §2 adds the `~/.config/cx/fleet-sessions` interface and the `CX_FLEET_VIA` switch, and §4 (plan.html#s4) adds the `Host fleet` ssh alias plus the `fleet-shell` RemoteCommand, while §2 keeps the superseded `srun` viewer alive ("CX_FLEET_VIA=srun keeps the step viewer for comparison"); neither section names anything it retires or merges, and the `srun` viewer is the one surface §8 already settled against

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the fleet behaviour is one deep module (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, 1355 lines) hiding session start, tab sizing, service supervision, reload and session-copy behind a small request protocol (`parse_request`/`handle_line`, `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:1166,1221`); the plan adds no parallel family of wrappers over it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan leaves the one fleet allocation with two records, two locks and two hold mechanisms (reckon's `placement.py` vs the fleet node's `fleet_node.py`/`cx`), and §6 names the unification action without naming which owner survives.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 (plan.html#s2) adds `~/.config/cx/fleet-sessions` and `CX_FLEET_VIA` and keeps both the ssh and the superseded `srun` viewer live ("CX_FLEET_VIA=srun keeps the step viewer for comparison") without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 (plan.html#s6, "Workers must be launched through the supervisor (reckon) … which needs a spawn request") proposes a new `spawn` request on the supervisor without citing reckon's existing worker-placement owner, `reckon/crew/placement.py`, which already places workers as `srun --overlap --jobid=<id>` steps inside this same allocation.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the login-side hold/resolve loop the plan places in `cx` (§2 "Holds one only if none runs") is a second, thin re-implementation of the ensure/one-allocation guarantee that reckon's `ensure_reservation` already owns, with no statement of why that owner cannot be extended.
